primaryLexicalAuthority.inspection: Extracted searchable text and visually inspected the relevant printed table pages; page numbering recorded as printed page and PDF page.

terms.tshivenda: ndifho ya vhubveledzi; synonym mutengo wa vhubveledzi
mutengo wa maragani; synonym mutengo wa maketeni

bindingCheck.limitation: This verifies the packet against exact source/current values and source-owner files, not native-language quality.

sesothoDitjeo.verdict: Lexically supported for production-cost contexts. DSAC lists `ditjeo tsa tlhahiso` for `cost of production`, so the candidate stem `ditjeo` is a defensible match. It does not establish every sentence-level use as fluent.

tshivendaTsengo.verdict: Do not accept `tsengo` yet. The inspected DSAC table gives `ndifho ya vhubveledzi` / `mutengo wa vhubveledzi` for production cost and `mutengo wa maragani` for market price; it does not establish the proposed generic `tsengo` as this lesson’s cost noun. Absence from this table is not proof the word is wrong. Keep only the source noun `cost`/`costs` in those slots until a language check confirms scope, preserving every other localized span.

xitsongaMaliUsed.verdict: The proposed `mali leyi tirhisiwaka` (“money being used”) risks narrowing economic costs to cash spent; the course separately includes labour, transport, sale costs and comparison with revenue. DSAC lists the more specific term `ntsengo wa andziso` for `cost of production`, but that alone does not validate the generic phrase in every context. Keep only the exact `cost`/`costs` noun in uncertain slots; retain translated framing and activity words. For the L1 body.11 composite candidate, use `ku humesa, ku paka ni ku xavisa costs` so the three cost categories remain explicit.

regularOrdersSesotho.verdict: No current mismatch confirmed. `Ditaelo tsa kamehla` can also be read as instructions, but this full source context is commercial: it connects customer orders, customers and growers, and keeping an agreement. That context supports the order sense. The proposal preserves “regular” and the source’s only-when/ability qualifier; do not hold the whole sentence based on isolated-word ambiguity.

productProduce.tshivendaProduct: `tshibveledzwa` is supported by DSAC as `final product`; using it for a customer’s market product is plausible. The plural `zwibveledzwa` is plausible for farm produce as goods, but the glossary does not directly verify every produce context.
productProduce.xitsongaProduct: DSAC uses `xikumiwa xo hetelela` for “final product”; it does not directly verify `xihumisiwa` as the buyer-facing noun `product`. Treat `xihumisiwa` as plausible but unverified. If needed, retain only `product` at those atomic noun slots while translating quantity/quality/delivery/payment around it.
productProduce.xitsongaProduce: `swihumisiwa` may mean things produced/outputs and is plausible in the market produce context; the inspected glossary does not settle this exact use. No defect is confirmed; local lexical review needed only for the noun, not the full sentence.

packingAndRelatedTerms.packingVerb: `ho paka` / `ku paka` in sentences about time and work plausibly translates the activity “packing”; no change needed from this spotcheck.
packingAndRelatedTerms.packagingNoun: In `keep suitable shade, packaging and storage through delivery`, `ho paka` / `ku paka` renders the act of packing, while source `packaging` may refer to the package/material/provision. This is a narrow unresolved composition risk in ST/TS body.6. If reviewers cannot confirm, keep only the noun `packaging` in English while retaining localized `shade`, `storage`, and `delivery`.

feesPaymentLosses.verdict: No confirmed meaning defect from these lexical candidates. Sesotho `tefo` for payment is supported contextually; Tshivenda `mbadelo` appears in the DSAC payment vocabulary; Xitsonga `ku hakela` is a verbal form that fits “day to pay” and the agreement list but should be locally checked for noun-style payment contexts. Sesotho `ditahlehelo` and Xitsonga `ku lahlekeriwa` are plausible losses; Tshivenda `ndozwo` has a related DSAC loss entry in a capital-loss context. Market fees remain English in some candidate rows where precision is uncertain. Preserve the distinct source categories fees, costs, selling price, money received, spoilage, unsold produce and losses.

highValueExamples.currentTarget: Dumellanang ka box contents, price, payment le se tla etsahala ha crops di haella. Regular orders di thusa ho rera feela ha customers le growers ba ka phethahatsa agreement.
highValueExamples.proposedTarget: Dumellanang ka tse ka mabokoseng, theko, tefo le se tla etsahala ha dijalo di haella. Ditaelo tsa kamehla di thusa ho rera feela ha bareki le balemi ba ka phethahatsa tumellano.

highValueExamples.sourceEnglish: Ask what the customer needs: product, quantity, quality, delivery and payment date.
highValueExamples.currentTarget: Vhudzisani uri mutengi u ṱoḓa mini: product, tshivhalo, quality, delivery na ḓuvha ḽa payment.
highValueExamples.proposedTarget: Vhudzisani uri mutengi u ṱoḓa mini: tshibveledzwa, tshivhalo, kwalithi, u isa na ḓuvha ḽa mbadelo.

highValueExamples.sourceEnglish: Ask what the customer needs: product, quantity, quality, delivery and payment date.
highValueExamples.currentTarget: Vutisa leswaku muxavi u lava yini: product, nhlayo, quality, delivery na siku ra ku hakela.
highValueExamples.proposedTarget: Vutisa leswaku muxavi u lava yini: xihumisiwa, nhlayo, khwalithi, ku yisa na siku ra ku hakela.

highValueExamples.sourceEnglish: Handle produce gently and keep suitable shade, packaging and storage through delivery.
highValueExamples.currentTarget: Khoma produce hi vukheta, u hlayisa ndzhuti lowu faneleke, packaging ni storage ku fikela loko yi fikisiwa.
highValueExamples.proposedTarget: Khoma swihumisiwa hi vukheta, u hlayisa ndzhuti lowu faneleke, ku paka ni ku hlayisa ku fikela loko swi fikisiwa.

highValueExamples.sourceEnglish: Handle produce gently and keep suitable shade, packaging and storage through delivery.
highValueExamples.currentTarget: Farani produce nga vhulenda, ni vhulunge nga shade yo teaho, packaging na storage u swika delivery i tshi fhela.
highValueExamples.proposedTarget: Farani zwibveledzwa nga vhulenda, ni vhulunge nga shade yo teaho, packaging na storage u swika delivery i tshi fhela.

highValueExamples.sourceEnglish: Compare costs and losses as well as selling price
highValueExamples.currentTarget: Pimanisa costs ni losses xikan’we ni selling price.
highValueExamples.proposedTarget: Pimanisa mali leyi tirhisiwaka ni ku lahlekeriwa xikan’we ni nxavo wo xavisa.

Candidate uses “ku paka” for “packaging”; same bounded noun/action ambiguity.

conclusion.recommendedEnglishHolds: Only the cost/costs noun at the listed Tshivenda/Xitsonga candidate slots if no direct language confirmation is available, plus potentially packaging as a noun in the two listed delivery sentences. Do not hold entire fields.
conclusion.safeCandidateAreas: Sesotho `ditjeo` has primary terminology support for production cost; Tshivenda `tshibveledzwa` has primary support for final product; customer/agreement context supports Sesotho `Ditaelo tsa kamehla` as order rather than command.
conclusion.notAFluentApproval: These primary term mappings support bounded lexical choices; they do not establish fluent, local farming, or market practice approval.
